cases.title: GNOME Wayland dual-GPU hard freeze
symptoms: hard freeze after enabling both i915 and nouveau
desktop becomes unusable during or shortly after graphical startup
signals: Nouveau RT_LINEAR_WITH_ZETA or DATA_ERROR storm after GNOME starts
cases.diagnosis: The catastrophic failure is in the Wayland multi-GPU desktop path, not proof that i915 initialization itself is broken.
safe_direction: force GDM to X11 with WaylandEnable=false
keep both kernel drivers available
postcheck for disappearance of the Wayland-specific error path
avoid: multiple unrelated GPU changes in the same reboot

cases.title: Single internal LCD appears twice and creates 2880x900 desktop
symptoms: desktop logical width is 2880 on a 1440x900 panel
pointer moves into a phantom second monitor
signals: xrandr shows two connected LVDS outputs
both GPUs are attached to Xorg providers
cases.diagnosis: The same physical panel is exposed through both GPUs in the muxed topology.
safe_direction: identify the duplicate output with xrandr
disable only the duplicate output for the current X11 session
prefer correct single-GPU display routing in the permanent architecture

cases.title: Chromium triggers Nouveau INVALID_VALUE errors
symptoms: high CPU in nouveau work queues
signals: chrome process owns NVIDIA render node
cases.diagnosis: Chromium/Nouveau is a reproducible error trigger; missing NVA5 firmware also prevents Nouveau video decode initialization.
safe_direction: correlate error timestamps with browser launch
prefer the stable renderer path while hybrid policy is being finalized
treat video-decode firmware failure separately from basic 3D acceleration

cases.title: Browser/ANGLE Intel failure incorrectly interpreted as broken i915
signals: host glxinfo or Mesa test selects i915/Crocus
cases.diagnosis: The failure is userspace/application-path-specific; Intel hardware acceleration is healthy on the reference machine.
safe_direction: validate Intel with browser-independent Mesa tools before changing drivers

cases.title: switcheroo-control marks NVIDIA as default even though Intel works
symptoms: Intel is present but not desktop default
cases.diagnosis: Default-GPU semantics follow firmware boot_vga on the reference system. This does not mean Intel or PRIME are unavailable.
safe_direction: separate firmware default semantics from Xorg PrimaryGPU and PRIME capability
continue toward a boot-safe Intel-primary policy without assuming boot_vga can be changed

cases.title: Intel-primary desktop with NVIDIA render offload
signals: Intel Crocus is default accelerated renderer
NVIDIA light 3D workload runs without new kernel faults
cases.diagnosis: The target rendering architecture is technically feasible on the reference MacBookPro6,2.
safe_direction: make display routing and Intel-primary selection boot-safe
retain explicit DRI_PRIME as the ground-truth NVIDIA offload path
test power management only after the display policy is stable

cases.title: Apple gpu-power-prefs EFI variable creation rejected
symptoms: attempt to force Intel as firmware boot GPU
signals: correct-format creation returns EINVAL / Invalid argument
cases.diagnosis: Runtime creation of gpu-power-prefs is not a reliable solution path on the reference machine.
safe_direction: do not retry automatically
use Linux gmux/Xorg policy instead
avoid: blind OpenCore NVRAM injection as a fallback

cases.title: Safe OpenCore update on an existing OCLP-flavoured EFI
symptoms: OpenCore needs updating without destroying an existing bootable EFI
signals: existing config contains OCLP-related NVRAM markers
staged files can be hash-compared before installation
cases.diagnosis: A component-level staged update is safer than replacing the complete EFI tree.
safe_direction: backup complete EFI
use matching ocvalidate.linux
stage outside ESP
validate config
update referenced components only
verify hashes and reboot before any unrelated GPU change
